Hi Patrícia, this is David. I am leaving this note because I do not want you to hear it from somebody else. Our contract comes up for renewal on the thirtieth of June, and the finance team here has been asking me hard questions since April. They have been talking to another vendor for about six weeks now, and last Thursday that vendor presented to my director. I am not telling you this to put pressure on you. I am telling you because I have been defending this platform inside my own company for two years, and at the moment I am running out of arguments. Two of my teams have not opened the dashboard since March, and when the numbers are that low, nobody in this building listens to me. So bring me something I can take to my director. Not a discount. Numbers, and a plan. Call me this week.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I have been looking at the Northwind account all morning, and I want to say two things before your call with David. First, do not open with the outage. That story is closed: you reported it in March and you did it well. Open with what has been happening since then, because that is what his numbers show. Usage has been falling for three months and two teams have been off the dashboard since the release. Say it out loud before he does. A customer trusts the person who names the problem first. Second, when you talk about the work, say it as something that has not stopped. We have been running weekly sessions since May is a completely different sentence from we ran some sessions in May. The first one tells him the work is still going on today, and that is exactly what he needs to take to his director. And put a number next to every claim. You have three days. Let me know how it goes.
